score.notes: A clean, symmetric front elevation with a clear tripartite reading: crimson studded plinth (base), a three-bay arched wall (middle), and a stepped gabled crown with a gold finial. The bay rhythm is deliberate — a taller central niche flanked by two matched panels, bracketed by four corner towers — so proportion reads as coherent rather than arbitrary, though the crown sits a touch small and lumpy atop the body and the corner towers are thin/stubby, which is why it stops short of inevitable. Color is the standout: a disciplined four-part scheme (royal lapis dominant, quartz-white supporting, gold accent, crimson base) with genuine hierarchy and harmony; it loses 'exceptional' only because the white begins to overtake the upper crown and dilute the identity. Detail is concentrated rather than pervasive — the three niches are nicely framed and recessed with gold ornament, and the plinth is studded, but the white inter-bay fields, the tower shafts, and the gable are flat, and the gold panel motifs read as somewhat crude plus/cross forms. Fidelity is solid: it unmistakably reads as a temple/shrine facade with central presence, a clear entrance niche, and a votive, vaguely ecclesiastical character — clear and characterful, but not a namable landmark.
